Item category probability curves

Source: R/item_cat_prob.R
RMitemCatProb.Rd

Plots the model's probability of each response category against the latent variable \(\theta\), one panel per item. The item parameters are estimated by conditional maximum likelihood with psychotools::pcmodel() (a dichotomous item is a 2-category partial credit model). The curves are coloured from low to high categories with a viridis palette. Comparable to eRm::plotICC() and the trace plots of mirt, with optional labels for items and categories.

Usage

RMitemCatProb(
  data,
  item_labels = NULL,
  category_labels = NULL,
  theta_range = NULL,
  n_points = 200L,
  viridis_option = "D",
  viridis_end = 0.95,
  vary_linetype = FALSE,
  facet_ncol = NULL,
  label_wrap = 25L,
  line_width = 0.9,
  font = "sans",
  output = c("ggplot", "dataframe"),
  label_curves = c("legend", "path"),
  item = NULL,
  text_size = 4
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses. Items must be scored starting at 0. Missing values (NA) are allowed, since CML uses the items each respondent answered.

item_labels

Optional character vector of descriptive item labels (facet strip titles). Must be the same length as ncol(data). If NULL (the default), column names are used.

category_labels

Optional character vector of labels for the response categories (legend). Must be the same length as the number of categories spanning from 0 to the maximum observed value. If NULL (the default), numeric category values are used.

theta_range

Numeric length 2. Range of the latent trait \(\theta\) (logits) plotted along the x-axis. When NULL (default) the range is c(-4, 4) for label_curves = "legend" and c(-5, 5) for label_curves = "path", which gives geomtextpath more room to place the labels at the peaks of the curves. Pass c(lo, hi) to override.

n_points

Integer. Number of evenly-spaced \(\theta\) values at which the curves are evaluated. Default 200L.

viridis_option

Character. Viridis palette identifier. One of "A" through "H". Default "D" (viridis green).

viridis_end

Numeric in (0, 1]. Upper end of the viridis palette range. Lower values keep the palette in its mid-tones and avoid the very bright yellow at 1.0. Default 0.95.

vary_linetype

Logical. If TRUE, each category also gets its own line type (solid for category 0, then increasingly broken dash patterns), so neighbouring curves stay apart in greyscale and for readers with colour vision deficiency. Default FALSE, colour only.

facet_ncol

Optional integer. Number of columns in the facet layout. Default NULL (ggplot2::facet_wrap() auto-layout).

label_wrap

Integer. Characters per line for facet-strip label wrapping. Default 25L.

line_width

Numeric. Line width for the probability curves. Default 0.9.

font

Character. Font family for all text. Default "sans".

output

Character. Either "ggplot" (default) for a ggplot object, or "dataframe" for the underlying long-format probability table.

label_curves

Character. How response categories are identified. "legend" (default) draws lines and a colour legend with one entry per category. "path" uses geomtextpath::geom_textpath() to write each category's label along its curve, as in classic trace plots, without a legend. It works for one item at a time, since narrow panels leave too little room for the labels. The model is still fitted on all items in data, as CML needs, and item selects the item to plot. Needs the optional geomtextpath package.

item

Character or integer. Used only when label_curves = "path". Either an item name (matching a column in data) or a column index, identifying which item's category curves to plot. Required for path mode.

text_size

Numeric. Used only when label_curves = "path". Size of the path labels in mm. Default 4.

Value

  • If output = "ggplot": a ggplot2::ggplot object, one facet per item.

  • If output = "dataframe": a long-format data.frame with columns Item (factor in column order), Category (integer), Theta and Probability, one row per item, category and grid value of theta.

Details

For each polytomous item i with response categories \(0, 1, \ldots, K_i\) and threshold parameters \(\delta_{i,1}, \ldots, \delta_{i,K_i}\) (CML, psychotools), the PCM category probability is

$$P(X_i = k \mid \theta) = \frac{\exp(\sum_{j=1}^{k} (\theta - \delta_{i,j}))}{\sum_{k'=0}^{K_i} \exp(\sum_{j=1}^{k'} (\theta - \delta_{i,j}))},$$

with the empty sum (when \(k = 0\)) taken as zero. A dichotomous item has a single threshold, its difficulty, which gives the usual logistic item characteristic curve.

The colours follow the category number, so low categories are at one end of the palette and high categories at the other. With vary_linetype = TRUE, the line types do too, and the legend shows colour and line type together. Thirteen line types are available, and they repeat beyond 13 categories. With category_labels, the legend shows those labels (for example "Never", "Sometimes", "Often").

An item with fewer categories than the others (for example one three-category item in a four-category scale) shows only its own categories. The y-axis still spans \([0, 1]\).

See also

RMtargeting() for the categories' ranges together with the person locations, RMitemHierarchy() for the threshold locations, RMitemCatFit() for a test of whether the categories work as scored, RMitemICCPlot() for conditional ICCs.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("eRm", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(pcmdat2, package = "eRm")

  # Default plot
  RMitemCatProb(pcmdat2)

  # Custom item and category labels
  RMitemCatProb(
    pcmdat2,
    item_labels     = c("Mood", "Sleep", "Appetite", "Energy"),
    category_labels = c("Never", "Sometimes", "Often")
  )

  # Underlying probability data
  df <- RMitemCatProb(pcmdat2, output = "dataframe")
  head(df)

  # One item with the labels written along the curves. The model is
  # still fitted on all four items, and `item` picks the one to plot.
  if (requireNamespace("geomtextpath", quietly = TRUE)) {
    RMitemCatProb(
      pcmdat2,
      category_labels = c("Never", "Sometimes", "Often"),
      label_curves    = "path",
      item            = "I1"
    )
  }
}

# }
